rationale: Anchor: statistical models, weighted by backtest error. GBT had the lowest backtest MAE at h3 (89.6) and its h0 median (796) matches the recent uptick; the seasonal analogue was best at h0 (98.3) and sits higher (892). No FluSight hub ensemble exists for this off-season week, so no ensemble prior. I started from the GBT medians (796/807/937/1189) and moved them up modestly to 830/870/960/1080: admissions have risen two weeks running (620→677→795, +17% last week) and national ILI has turned up from its July floor (0.87→0.94→1.11, +18% wk/wk), consistent with an early 2026-27 season start rather than noise; the provisional last week also tends to revise upward. I did not take the full seasonal-analogue level because the 2025-26 season only began rising in mid-October, so calendar-week analogues overstate near-term growth. Intervals are lognormal, right-skewed, and widened well beyond the model backtest intervals (e.g. h3 700-1710 vs GBT 797-1775) because we are near a possible seasonal inflection where flu can turn faster than it looks, and the backtest intervals assume the near future resembles the recent flat summer. I would revise upward if ILI keeps doubling its weekly growth or if state-level admissions show a sustained multi-week rise; downward if the uptick stalls and ILI reverts to ~0.9.
